---
title: "Convergence diagnostics"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---

Use `convergence = "auto"` for the default core-only behavior, `"none"` to
disable formal capture, `"core"` to explicitly request the five trait traces,
or `"extended"` for applicable covariance, probability, sampled
`selection_s`, annotation, and selected-marker quantities.

The core quantities are `vbs`, `vgs`, `ves`, `vle`, and `vld`. Formal traces
are genuine unpooled logical-chain states captured after burn-in at every
iteration. They are not thinned by `nthin` and are independent of compact
chain retention.

The shared summary reports rank-normalized split/folded R-hat, bulk and tail
ESS, mean ESS where available, posterior SD, MCSE of the posterior mean, and
relative mean MCSE. Threshold warnings are advisory and aggregated.

```r
fit <- stblr_csr(
  stats, Glist,
  method = "sbayesr",
  nchains = 4,
  convergence = "extended",
  convergence_control = list(
    extended_groups = c("probability", "selection_s"),
    selected_markers = c("rs1", "rs25"),
    selected_marker_quantities = c("b", "d", "component"),
    keep_traces = TRUE,
    max_trace_gb = 1,
    allow_large_traces = FALSE
  )
)
```

`selected_markers` must be explicit IDs or one-based indices; `NULL` is not
all markers. Trace memory is estimated before sampling. Oversized requests
fail unless `allow_large_traces = TRUE`, in which case one warning is issued
without silently dropping or thinning quantities.

Inspect `fit$convergence$overview`, the scalar summary, and—when retained—
`fit$convergence_traces`. `keep_chains` and `keep_traces` serve different
purposes. Diagnostics assess chain mixing; passing thresholds does not prove
model correctness, posterior calibration, or convergence in an absolute sense.

Implementation details are in the
[convergence contract](../dev/blr_convergence_contract.md).
